    "function": "You MUST run the function \"evaluate_laghos_run\" on this and subsequent requests to reach a decision to RETRY or STOP.\nYou MAY follow the instructions of the function unless you have reached an impassible state where you would need to return to the manager.\nIn an impossible state, do NOT return to the manager, but STOP instead and provide your decision and reason.\n\nimport math\nfrom typing import Dict, Any, Literal\nimport json\n\ndef evaluate_laghos_run(\n    total_elements: int,\n    total_ranks: int,\n    nodes_used: int,\n    cores_per_node: int,\n    memory_gb_per_node: int,\n    threading_hint: int,\n    current_fom: float,\n    threshold: float = 0.90,\n    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 1.5e6,\n    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 35000.0,\n    elements_per_gb: float = 1.0e6,\n    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Evaluates a Laghos run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.\n\n    This function acts as a \"diagnostician\" by analyzing the performance of a\n    completed Laghos run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most\n    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and\n    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.\n\n    Args:\n        total_elements (int): The total number of mesh elements in the simulation.\n        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.\n        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.\n        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.\n        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.\n        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).\n        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in FOM/second.\n        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).\n        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 1.5e6 FOM/sec).\n        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for elements/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 35,000).\n        elements_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (elements per GB of RAM, default 1.0e6).\n        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).\n\n    Returns:\n        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.\n    \"\"\"\n    if total_ranks == 0:\n        return {\"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": \"The number of tasks cannot be zero.\", \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\"}\n\n    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---\n    elements_per_rank = total_elements / total_ranks\n    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node\n    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank\n    \n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(elements_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used\n\n    performance_ratio = 0.0\n    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:\n        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    estimated_memory_gb = total_elements / elements_per_gb\n    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0\n    \n    metrics = {\n        \"performance_ratio\": round(performance_ratio, 3),\n        \"scaling_efficiency\": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),\n        \"memory_utilization\": round(memory_utilization, 3),\n        \"elements_per_rank\": int(elements_per_rank),\n        \"theoretical_max_fom_per_sec\": f\"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}\"\n    }\n\n    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---\n    \n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of elements is too large for the allocated memory.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"DECREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for \"low\" efficiency\n         return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of elements per rank is too small (communication-bound).\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n        \"reason\": f\"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.\",\n        \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n        \"metrics\": metrics\n    }\n"

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" install && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version to enable MPI capabilities.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version to enable MPI capabilities.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version and explicitly enable METIS and Hypre support
    # to ensure the build system can find their headers and libraries.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' step does not install HYPRE_config.h, so we copy it manually.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,

# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #

    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \

    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    # Manually copy headers, as 'make install' may not place them in the top-level include path.
    cp HYPRE_config.h hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----

    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,

    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide HYPRE_INC_DIR to locate its namespaced headers.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local HYPRE_INC_DIR=/usr/local/include/hypre && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide HYPRE_INCLUDE_DIR to locate its namespaced headers.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local HYPRE_INCLUDE_DIR=/usr/local/include/hypre && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We inject the Hypre include path via CXXFLAGS to ensure it's picked up by
    # all parts of MFEM's complex build system, including configuration sub-makes.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local CXXFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include/hypre" && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.

    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.

ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.

# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.

    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \

    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \

    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \

    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]

# Dockerfile for the Laghos HPC application
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its modern toolchain and package availability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend and a standard timezone to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, networking utilities,
# and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget).
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments. These settings are crucial for
# stability and performance within schedulers like Kubernetes.
# OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT is necessary as we are operating as the root user.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Add the standard location for locally installed libraries to the linker path.
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# This single RUN command builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach minimizes layer count and final image size by performing all build
# and cleanup operations within a single Docker build layer.
RUN BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    #
    # ---- 1. Build METIS 4.0.3 ----
    # This is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The specified OPTFLAGS are required to avoid build errors with modern GCC versions.
    # Its Makefile lacks an 'install' target, so we manually copy the artifacts.
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0 ----
    # This is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    # Fortran is disabled and bigint is enabled as per requirements.
    # The 'make install' command correctly installs all necessary files.
    #
    echo "Building Hypre..." && \
    wget -qO - https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzvf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    #
    # ---- 3. Build MFEM 4.7 ----
    # The core Finite Element Method library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel version, explicitly enable METIS/Hypre support,
    # and provide the HYPRE_DIR path to its standard install location.
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    #
    # ---- 4. Build Laghos ----
    # The main application. We must point its Makefile to our locally built MFEM library.
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    #
    # ---- 5. Finalize Image ----
    # Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # Copy the required data files to the runtime WORKDIR.
    #
    echo "Finalizing image..." && \
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    #
    # ---- 6. Cleanup ----
    # Remove the entire build directory to minimize the final image size.
    #
    echo "Cleaning up build artifacts..." && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default command to run when the container starts.
# Displaying the help message is a good default for HPC applications.
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]
